--- BEGIN SOURCE: museum-pilot.md ---

# Museum visitor note: an indoor route when the sculpture garden floods

This note is for visitors whose plans included the sculpture garden. When the
garden closes for high water, the front desk can give visitors a free printed
route through the permanent indoor sculpture galleries. The route starts at
the front desk and ends at the café. It follows step-free public corridors.
Visitors should still check the same-day garden notice before travelling.

In April, the museum handed out the route at two wet Sunday openings. The
desk counted 38 copies handed out. At the first opening some visitors asked
where to start, so a sign was added by the desk at the second. Staff recorded
no systematic counts of how many visitors completed the route and did not
track visitor satisfaction. The note is intended to help visitors adapt their
visit when the garden is closed. There is no plan to replace the garden visit
permanently.

--- END SOURCE: museum-pilot.md ---

idea.title: A pilot without measurement: the museum distributed an alternative route but didn't track whether it worked
idea.description: The museum ran a small, on‑the‑ground pilot—handing out a free printed indoor route when the sculpture garden closed for high water—but staff recorded distribution counts only and did not measure route completion or visitor satisfaction, limiting what can be learned from the experiment.
idea.audience: Museum operations managers, visitor experience leads, program evaluators at cultural institutions
idea.rationale: This idea highlights a concrete operational learning: running a pilot without clear success metrics prevents evidence‑based decisions about whether the intervention should be refined, repeated, or scaled. It matters to readers who run visitor experiments because it shows how easy it is to miss the evaluation step even when a feasible intervention is deployed. Gaps & uncertainty: the source documents the absence of systematic completion and satisfaction tracking but does not state whether informal feedback was collected or whether any internal follow‑up evaluation was planned.
idea.evidence: Explicit facts: the museum handed out the route at two wet Sunday openings and the desk counted 38 copies handed out; “staff recorded no systematic counts of how many visitors completed the route and did not track visitor satisfaction.”
